title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Uroskopie-Rad als Beobachtung-Diagnose-Therapie-Kette
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: Mittelalterliche Urinräder verbinden sichtbare Farb-/Ringmerkmale mit Diagnose und teils Behandlung; f68r1s Zentrum-plus-28 Karten könnte ein solches mehrstufiges Nachschlagewerk tragen, obwohl die abweichende Kardinalität ein harter Gegenpunkt ist.

design.scope_description: Nur die bereits gebundene f68r1-Zählung (ein Zentrum plus 28 Randgruppen) und vorhandene Quellenkarten; keine neue Bild- oder Textfreigabe.
design.mechanism: A visual sign selects a diagnostic record, which may then select a condition or treatment note; the same item is therefore a lookup key, not necessarily the diagnosis itself.
design.unit: The central group and 28 peripheral f68r1 groups in the existing locus record, compared as a complete diagram rather than isolated word glosses.
design.contrast: Mehrstufiges diagnostisches Nachschlagewerk versus gleichförmiger räumlicher Katalog.
design.prediction: The uroscopy model predicts one fixed sign-to-diagnosis relation and a second, separately structured diagnosis-to-action/result relation. The plain-catalog model predicts uniform peer slots and no second-stage cross-reference.
concrete_observations: HIST:2797fab43dce948f records one central plus 28 noncentral f68r1 labels; no meanings are independently bound.

QMUL's primary-witness edition describes late-fifteenth-century entries as repeated `Urine as [colour] [optional comparative] [resulting diagnosis]` units, while the Durham Cosin MS V.iv.7 catalogue records a wheel with 20 urine bottles and an inner band of seven digestive-significance circles linked by lines, with a recipe at each page foot.
The 28-versus-20/7 cardinality mismatch is retained as an explicit source conflict, not repaired by merging slots.
linked_consequences: A diagnostic-wheel reading requires a stable second-layer relation: changing the outer sign class should select a constrained inner condition/result class rather than an arbitrary neighboring label.
It predicts an exceptional central role or entry/healthy baseline only if the bound centre has a relation not shared by all 28 peripheral groups; otherwise the catalogue rival remains live.
A plain catalogue permits every peripheral group to be an equal independent label and predicts no cross-layer reuse or condition-to-treatment continuation.
design.nearest_rival: A spatial 29-entry star or calendar catalogue whose centre is simply one peer and whose apparent inner/outer relation is layout only.
design.distinguishing_observation: Freeze the existing centre/rim and any already recorded inner relations, then test whether two different outer groups share a constrained downstream class while preserving the same position rule. A position-only catalogue should not produce a repeatable two-stage mapping.
assumption_costs: A late medieval uroscopy layout is a structural analogue, not a Voynich lexical key.
The f68r1 centre/rim ownership is reliable in the existing source record.
A diagnosis/action layer must be visible in bound relations; no missing arrows or meanings may be supplied.
design.strongest_likely_failure: The witness's 20-bottle plus seven-circle architecture does not match f68r1's 28 rim groups, and no author-visible f68r1 cross-layer links are currently bound; the analogy could be numerology over a spatial catalogue.

primary_sources.locator: late-fifteenth-century William Bokynham tract, edition overview
primary_sources.source_consequence: Repeated colour-led entries join an observable sign to a resulting diagnosis.

primary_sources.locator: Cosin MS V.iv.7, Tabula de iudiciis vrinarum per colores
primary_sources.source_consequence: A wheel separates a bottle/colour band, seven inner digestive-significance circles and foot recipes.
